name: Sonnet small/mid-cap growth
strategy: Concentrated long book in secular small/mid-cap growth (small-cap beta, semis leverage, fintech, space, biotech) with a large cash cushion, tilted toward names with intact fundamentals over pure beta and trimmed ahead of known event risk.
reassessment_note: WebSearch budget was already exhausted for this session (200/200), so this week's research was done via WebFetch (AI-summarized fetches of Yahoo Finance pages), not live search -- noting that per the brief's instruction. Three real changes from last week's leg: (1) IWM's broad small-cap beta is fighting a genuine macro headwind right now -- Russell 2000 has been described as under 'constant weakness since late August' with Treasury yields and crude both grinding higher, and the ETF is -5.37% over the trailing month -- so I'm trimming the pure-beta leg rather than holding it at prior size. (2) SOFI is down -35% YTD with earnings on 2026-10-27, close enough to introduce event risk before this leg would mark again; fundamentals (revenue +41% YoY) are fine but analyst sentiment is explicitly mixed on credit risk/valuation, so I'm cutting size rather than exiting. (3) RKLB's -18% one-month drawdown is a dilutive-equity-raise reaction, not a broken thesis -- the raise left the company with $2.3B cash and a fresh $870M Iridium contract, Raymond James just initiated Outperform, and the average street target implies ~69% upside from here -- so I'm adding to the dip. HOOD is the standout performer (fundamentals plus a +9% single-day move on 9/18, analysts still raising targets) so I'm sizing it up modestly. SOXL stays at prior size and stop/TP (leveraged semis exposure, no new signal either way). XBI trimmed slightly -- still a believer in the biotech laggard-turning-up story but conviction is currently softer than RKLB/HOOD, and the leg remains in drawdown with no fresh positive catalyst found. Net effect: gross exposure drops from 47% to 46% and cash rises slightly to 54%, reflecting a mild risk-off tilt given the macro backdrop while rotating dollars from the weakest-conviction legs (IWM, SOFI, XBI) into the strongest-conviction ones (HOOD, RKLB).

positions.thesis: Trimmed from 13% to 9%. Pure small-cap beta exposure, and the tape right now is a genuine headwind for that beta specifically: Russell 2000 has been described as showing 'constant weakness since late August' with crude oil and Treasury yields grinding higher almost daily while major indices drift lower erratically -- IWM is -5.37% over the trailing month even though it's still +16.74% YTD. Keeping a reduced position rather than exiting because the longer-run uptrend and relative outperformance vs the small-blend category (16.74% vs 12.09%) are still intact; adding a 12% stop that wasn't on this leg before, given the leg is now fighting the macro tape rather than riding it.

Unchanged size and risk brackets. 3x leveraged semis exposure to the AI-capex buildout theme that underpins this book's growth mandate; the prior leg is flat-to-slightly-positive (+0.32%) and I found no fresh negative catalyst this week, so I'm leaving the existing stop/TP discipline in place rather than churning a working position.

Trimmed from 6% to 4% ahead of the 2026-10-27 earnings date. Fundamentals remain genuinely strong -- 41% adjusted net-revenue growth, 35% customer growth, $14.8B in loan originations, a 12.99% profit margin -- and the average analyst target of $20.34 implies roughly 20% upside from the current $16.96 mark. But the stock is down 35% YTD and analyst commentary explicitly flags credit-risk and valuation concerns, and an earnings print is close enough to the horizon that I'd rather hold a smaller position into it than the prior 6%.

Increased from 5% to 8%, buying the dip. RKLB is down 18.4% over the trailing month and 4.8% on 9/18 alone, but the proximate cause is a $1.94B dilutive equity offering, not a broken business -- the raise left the balance sheet with $2.3B in cash, the company just signed an $870M Iridium contract and successfully completed its 96th Electron launch, and revenue is still growing ~62% YoY. Raymond James initiated coverage Outperform ($80 PT) on 9/11 and the average street target of $109.37 implies ~69% upside from the current $64.57 mark. Losing the NASA StarBurst mission to SpaceX is a real competitive headwind worth noting, but doesn't change the core small-cap space-growth thesis for this book. Keeping the wide 20% stop given the name's volatility.

Increased from 10% to 13%, sizing up the book's best-performing and best-supported leg. HOOD surged 9.12% on 9/18 on continued fundamental strength -- $1.31B Q2 revenue at a 42.9% margin, and the company is projected to exceed $500B in customer assets by 2027. Deutsche Bank just raised its target from $136 to $138 (Buy) and Bernstein rates it Outperform (85/100). There's a modest known overhang (an insider-trading-charge headline caused a prior 5% pullback, and the CFO sold ~$1.3M of stock), but that's already reflected in the mark and doesn't offset the broader trend of rising targets and strong execution. Keeping the existing stop/TP brackets given they've been appropriate through this leg's run.

Trimmed from 7% to 6%. Still hold the secular small/mid-cap biotech thesis (sector underinvestment reversing eventually), but this leg remains in drawdown (-3.22%) and I did not turn up a fresh positive catalyst this week to justify holding it at full prior size while reallocating toward higher-conviction legs (HOOD, RKLB). Not exiting -- the biotech laggard-turning-up story is a real, if currently unconfirmed, part of this book's mandate.
